title: Divergence: kani::is_under_bound_failure misclassifies a real L2 counterexample as UnderBound (degrades a disproved contract to L1 — R-DEFER-9 anti-cheat hole)

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content:
Failing test (the fixer must place it in forge/src/kani.rs mod tests — the symbols classify_l2_outcome/L2Result/is_under_bound_failure are private to the binary-only forge crate) supplied at forge/tests/divergence_degrade_oq2_pending.rs.pending.

DIVERGENCE: forge/src/kani.rs `is_under_bound_failure` — second arm `d.contains("unwind")` is a bare-substring match on the user's ens clause text, which kani echoes verbatim into `Failed Checks:` (parse_failed_checks). A REAL L2 counterexample whose ens text contains the substring 'unwind' (e.g. spec helper unwind_count, field .unwind, rewind, unwound) → classify_l2_outcome returns UnderBound → run_ladder degrades the DISPROVED contract to L1 with a lowered-assurance stamp. This hides a real bug behind a certified rung — the R-DEFER-9 / REQ-2 anti-cheat failure OQ-2 calls 'the sharpest hole'.

AUTHORITY: .design/forge/degrade-ladder.md OQ-2 — 'a concrete Failed Checks: assertion failed: <ens clause> = counterexample; unwinding assertion loop N = under-bound/inconclusive'; ratified resolution favors R-DEFER-9 (ambiguous → Counterexample). The under-bound discriminator must be kani's boilerplate 'unwinding assertion' ONLY.

CONFIRMED deterministically (faithful copy of 2323dcb logic): input 'assertion failed: result == unwind_count(n)' → UnderBound (WRONG); control 'assertion failed: result == spec_sum(xs)' → Counterexample (right).

EXPECTED FIX: drop the `|| d.contains("unwind")` arm; key on `unwinding assertion` only.

Note: a binary-only crate has no external pin for a private fn; the test belongs inside kani.rs alongside the one-line fix (the critic cannot Edit production code).

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Critic pin of the OQ-2 divergence: commit the failing-test artifact (forge/tests/divergence_degrade_oq2_pending.rs.pending) documenting that kani::is_under_bound_failure's bare 'unwind' substring arm degrades a real L2 counterexample to L1. The runnable test targets a private symbol of the binary-only forge crate, so it lands inside kani.rs mod tests with the fixer's one-line fix (drop the || d.contains("unwind") arm). No production code edited by the critic.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content:
FIXED at de890e1 (single file forge/src/kani.rs + removed .pending).

ROOT CAUSE removed: fn is_under_bound_failure second arm '|| d.contains("unwind")' (bare-substring match on the ens clause kani echoes into Failed Checks:). Now keys on kani's BOILERPLATE 'unwinding assertion' ONLY.
  before: d.contains("unwinding assertion") || d.contains("unwind")
  after:  d.contains("unwinding assertion")

The unwind-substring counterexample now classifies Counterexample: new in-kani.rs test classify_l2_assertion_with_unwind_substring_is_counterexample ('assertion failed: result == unwind_count(n)' -> Counterexample, hard fail, not UnderBound->L1). The genuine pure-unwinding under-bound ('unwinding assertion loop N') STILL -> UnderBound -> L1 (matches via 'unwinding assertion'); classify_l2_unwinding_assertion_is_under_bound + degrade::l2_under_bound_drops_to_l1 stay green.

GAUNTLET: cargo test -p forge 119 + suites 0 failed; cargo test --workspace 0 failed; clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings PASS; fmt --all --check PASS. No conformance fixtures/assertions touched (R-CHAR-3). .pending artifact removed.
